title.en: Magnetic field, field lines and the field due to a current

text.en: A compass needle moves near a wire carrying current. Hans Christian Oersted noticed this in 1820, showing that electricity and magnetism are linked.

A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force can be felt. Field lines go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.
Field lines never cross each other, and closer lines mean a stronger field.
A current-carrying straight wire produces circular field lines around it. The direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule.
Hold the wire in your right hand with the thumb along the current; the curled fingers show the field direction.
A circular loop gives field lines that are concentric near the wire and straight at the centre. A coil of many turns increases the strength.
A solenoid is a long coil. Its field is like that of a bar magnet, uniform inside, and an iron core makes an electromagnet.
The field increases with current and with the number of turns.
Electromagnets are used in cranes, electric bells and relays.

problem.en: What happens to the magnetic field when the current in a solenoid is doubled?

text.en: The field strength depends on the current.
Doubling the current doubles the strength.
Increasing the turns would also strengthen it.

prompt.en: How is a magnetic field related to electric current?

points.en: Field lines come out of N and enter S; they never cross.
Right-hand thumb rule gives the direction around a straight wire.
A solenoid with an iron core is an electromagnet.
